articleTitle: Energy restriction and iron supplementation improve iron status in women with obesity regardless of red meat consumption: a randomized controlled trial.
takeaways: Women with obesity and iron deficiency without anemia saw serum iron levels increase by 25% (from 55.8 to 69.8 μg/dL) on a low-calorie, high-protein diet with iron supplementation over 60 days
Adding red meat to a low-calorie diet provided no additional iron status benefits compared to the same diet without red meat when combined with oral iron supplements
A 60-day low-calorie, high-protein diet with iron supplementation improved multiple markers including ferritin, transferrin, and reduced fat mass regardless of red meat inclusion
Women following the non-red meat diet showed a 17% increase in serum iron levels (from 65.3 to 76.8 μg/dL) over 60 days with calorie restriction and iron supplementation
